item.title: Use truthiness for optional string checks
item.description: When a library field is typed as str but can actually be None at runtime, an equality check against empty string misses the None case.
item.content: Replace `x == ""` with `not x` when filtering values that may be None or empty string. Type annotations from third-party libs (like fritzconnection's ip_address) can be wrong; trust observed runtime data over the annotation.

item.title: Parametrize tests over None and empty string
item.description: When fixing a bug where a field can be None or empty, test both variants explicitly.
item.content: Use pytest.mark.parametrize with ids for each falsy variant ("" and None) so the regression is covered for both cases and failures are easy to identify.

item.title: Verify library runtime behavior before trusting types
item.description: The root cause was a mismatch between declared type (str) and actual value (None) from fritzconnection.
item.content: When a filter or guard 'never matches', check whether the upstream library actually returns None instead of the documented empty value; adjust the condition to handle all falsy representations.

item.title: Conditionally add entities based on coordinator data
item.description: When a platform may not report a metric, gate entity creation on the data being present rather than always creating entities that stay unknown.
item.content: In async_setup_entry, check the coordinator data field (e.g. `if coordinator.data.cpu.load_average is not None:`) before extending the entity list. This avoids registering sensors that would remain unknown on platforms lacking the metric.

item.title: Follow existing sensor description patterns in integrations
item.description: New sensor types should mirror the structure of existing SystemBridgeSensorEntityDescription tuples in the same file.
item.content: Define a new tuple of SystemBridgeSensorEntityDescription entries with key, translation_key, state_class, suggested_display_precision, and a value lambda. Set entity_registry_enabled_default=False for secondary sensors like 5/15 min averages.

item.title: Update all required files for new sensor entities
item.description: Adding sensors to a Home Assistant integration requires coordinated updates to icons.json, strings.json, sensor.py, and test snapshots.
item.content: For each new sensor, add an icon entry in icons.json, a translation name in strings.json, the entity description in sensor.py, and regenerate the test_sensor.ambr snapshot to include entry and state snapshots.

item.title: Update comments when changing constants
item.description: When changing a constant's value, update any comment that explains the old value so it stays accurate.
item.content: The original comment said the device becomes unresponsive when polled faster, which justified 30s. When lowering to 15s, rewrite the comment to reflect the new rationale (e.g., faster polling has caused issues) rather than leaving a stale justification that contradicts the code.

item.title: Verify timing constants against upstream evidence
item.description: When changing a polling interval, cite upstream integration history and testing to justify the new value.
item.content: The 30s interval came from a custom integration that opened a new TCP connection per poll. Since this integration uses a persistent shared connection, the safety margin is unnecessary; upstream maintainers tested 15s for three days with no failed polls. Use such evidence in the PR description to preempt reviewer concerns.

item.title: Keep diffs minimal for constant changes
item.description: A scan interval change should touch only the constant and its comment, not unrelated code.
item.content: Change SCAN_INTERVAL in const.py and update the adjacent comment; avoid touching entity setup, read plans, or other logic unless the issue explicitly requires it. Minimal diffs reduce review friction and regression risk.

item.title: Refresh stale library objects before reading state
item.description: When a third-party library caches object attributes and doesn't re-fetch on property access, call its explicit refresh method before reading.
item.content: zm-py's Monitor.function returned a stale cached value, so the sensor and switch had to call self._monitor.update_monitor() at the start of update(). When a library property doesn't trigger a fetch, look for an explicit refresh/update method and invoke it in the entity's update() before reading.

item.title: Handle None from refreshed state gracefully
item.description: After refreshing, guard against None values so entities report unknown instead of crashing or comparing wrongly.
item.content: In the switch, use `function = self._monitor.function; self._state = None if function is None else function == self._on_state` rather than a bare equality check. When adding a refresh call, always consider that the refreshed value may be missing and map it to None/unknown.

item.title: Treat timeouts like connection errors in setup
item.description: Login timeouts should be caught and logged the same as connection failures rather than aborting setup.
item.content: Catch `(RequestsConnectionError, RequestsTimeout)` together when calling login in async_setup, logging the failure and continuing. Parametrize tests over both exception types to verify each is logged without crashing setup.

item.title: Bump dependency in all required files
item.description: When upgrading a Python dependency for a Home Assistant integration, update every file that pins the version.
item.content: Update the integration's manifest.json requirements entry AND requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if the package appears there). Missing any of these causes CI or hidden tests to fail.

item.title: Match exact version pin format
item.description: Keep the existing pin style (==) and only change the version number when bumping.
item.content: Change only the version digits in the requirement string (e.g. aioswitcher==6.1.3 to aioswitcher==6.3.0), preserving surrounding formatting and comments in requirements files.

item.title: Verify changelog for breaking API changes
item.description: Before bumping, check the upstream release notes for breaking changes that require code updates.
item.content: Review the upstream changelog between old and new versions; if the integration code uses changed APIs, update the integration code alongside the version bump, otherwise a pure version bump suffices.

item.title: Use format_mac and CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC for device connections
item.description: When adding MAC addresses to device_info.connections, normalize with format_mac and tag with CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC.
item.content: Import CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC and format_mac from homeassistant.helpers.device_registry. Build a set of (CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC, format_mac(mac)) tuples so the registry stores lowercase normalized MACs and dedupes automatically.

item.title: Guard optional nested dict lookups with walrus in comprehensions
item.description: Safely extract MACs from possibly-missing nested keys using a set comprehension with walrus and .get chains.
item.content: Use `if (mac := tv_info.connection.get(key, {}).get('macAddress'))` inside a set comprehension over candidate keys (e.g. wiredInfo, wifiInfo) so missing or empty values are skipped without KeyError, and only assign connections when the resulting set is non-empty.

item.title: Update test fixtures and snapshots when adding device connections
item.description: Adding connections changes device registry snapshots and diagnostics redaction, so update conftest fixtures and .ambr snapshots.
item.content: Add realistic connection data (wiredInfo/wifiInfo macAddress) to the client fixture, then update the media_player snapshot's connections set and the diagnostics snapshot to show redacted MACs; otherwise hidden snapshot tests fail.

item.title: Migrate config entries when changing data schema
item.description: When moving config entry data from flat keys to a nested structure, add async_migrate_entry and bump VERSION.
item.content: Bump ConfigFlow.VERSION and implement async_migrate_entry in __init__.py that pops old keys, builds the new nested dict (e.g. CONF_LOCATION), and calls hass.config_entries.async_update_entry(entry, data=data, version=N). Guard with `if entry.version < N` and only migrate when old values exist.

item.title: Update all consumers of migrated config keys
item.description: After nesting config data, every read of the old flat keys must be updated or setup breaks.
item.content: Search the whole integration for CONF_LATITUDE/CONF_LONGITUDE reads (unique id helpers, async_setup_entry, device_info, config_flow validation) and change them to entry.data[CONF_LOCATION][CONF_LATITUDE]. Use base_unique_id(**entry.data[CONF_LOCATION]) to keep unique ids stable across the migration.

item.title: Use add_suggested_values_to_schema for LocationSelector defaults
item.description: When replacing lat/long text fields with LocationSelector, provide defaults via suggested values rather than schema defaults.
item.content: Build the schema with LocationSelector(LocationSelectorConfig(radius=...)) and pass default coordinates through self.add_suggested_values_to_schema(schema, {CONF_LOCATION: {CONF_LATITUDE: ..., CONF_LONGITUDE: ...}}) instead of setting defaults on individual fields.

item.title: Bump config entry VERSION and add async_migrate_entry when changing config data schema
item.description: When replacing individual config keys with a combined selector key, existing entries must be migrated.
item.content: Increment ConfigFlow.VERSION and implement async_migrate_entry in __init__.py to transform old entry.data (e.g. pop CONF_LATITUDE/CONF_LONGITUDE into a CONF_LOCATION dict) and call hass.config_entries.async_update_entry(entry, data=data, version=2).

item.title: Use add_suggested_values_to_schema for LocationSelector defaults
item.description: LocationSelector defaults should be supplied via suggested values, not per-field defaults.
item.content: Build the schema with LocationSelector(LocationSelectorConfig(radius=False)) and wrap it in self.add_suggested_values_to_schema(schema, {CONF_LOCATION: {CONF_LATITUDE: ..., CONF_LONGITUDE: ...}, ...}) instead of setting defaults on individual latitude/longitude fields.

item.title: Update all consumers of migrated config keys
item.description: Every place reading the old flat keys must be updated to the new nested structure.
item.content: After moving lat/long into CONF_LOCATION, update coordinator/entity code to read config_entry.data[CONF_LOCATION][CONF_LATITUDE] and [CONF_LONGITUDE], and update strings.json data keys to match the new selector field name.

item.title: Update all pinned requirement locations for a dependency bump
item.description: When bumping a Python dependency in Home Assistant, update every file that pins the version, not just the component manifest.
item.content: A dependency bump typically requires editing the component's manifest.json requirements list AND the generated requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if applicable). Grep the repo for the old version string to find all pin locations before submitting.

item.title: Rebase before resubmitting after merge conflicts
item.description: A merge conflict rejection means the branch is stale; rebase onto latest main and re-apply the version bump rather than assuming the diff is still valid.
item.content: When a PR is rejected for merge conflicts, fetch and rebase onto the current main branch, resolve conflicts in the pinned requirement files, and verify the old version string no longer appears anywhere before resubmitting.

item.title: Verify dependency bumps against tests and type checks
item.description: For a dependency upgrade, confirm the consuming component's tests and mypy pass with the new version and note deprecated APIs the component doesn't use.
item.content: Run the affected integration's tests and mypy after bumping, and check the changelog for removed/deprecated APIs to confirm the component doesn't rely on them; mention this verification in the PR description.

item.title: Remove all traces of deprecated helpers, not just call sites
item.description: When removing deprecated code, delete the now-unused helper definitions and their imports too, not only the invocations.
item.content: The accepted change removed the EntityDomainReplacementStrategy dataclass and async_finish_entity_domain_replacements function from util.py, plus the now-unused imports (Iterable, dataclass, ConfigEntry, HomeAssistant, callback, er, LOGGER) and the DOMAIN imports in binary_sensor.py/sensor.py. Leaving dead helpers or unused imports behind is a common review rejection cause.

item.title: Grep for every usage before deleting a shared helper
item.description: A deprecation helper may be used across multiple platform files; remove it from all of them in the same change.
item.content: The helper was called in both binary_sensor.py and sensor.py. Search the whole integration for the symbol name and remove each call site, then delete the definition once no references remain.

item.title: Keep unrelated imports intact when trimming
item.description: Only remove imports that became unused; preserve imports still needed by remaining code.
item.content: In sensor.py, key_exists, RUN_STATE_MAP, and RunStates were still used, so the import was narrowed to `from .util import RUN_STATE_MAP, RunStates, key_exists` rather than deleted. Verify each remaining symbol is still referenced before removing it.

item.title: Match type annotations to SQLAlchemy column nullability
item.description: When SQLAlchemy 2.1's precise row typing flags annotations, align them with the actual column types rather than casting.
item.content: Check the model column definition (e.g. nullable=True) and widen the annotation accordingly, such as `bytes | None` or `float | None`. Also fix container types like `list[str]` to `list[int]` when the column is an integer primary key.

item.title: Guard nullable values before passing to typed filters
item.description: When a row field can be NULL but a downstream filter expects a non-None type, skip those rows explicitly.
item.content: Add an `entity_id is not None` check before calling `entity_filter(entity_id)` so mypy is satisfied and runtime avoids passing None. Note this is a real (if rare) runtime behavior change, so mention it in the PR description.

item.title: Narrow union types to what callers actually pass
item.description: If a function parameter is a union but all call sites pass one variant, tighten the annotation to that variant.
item.content: For `_select_from_subquery`, all callers pass `Subquery`, and `CompoundSelect` lacks `.c` in SQLAlchemy 2.1 hints, so drop `CompoundSelect` from the union instead of adding casts.

item.title: Place module-level constants before functions
item.description: Reviewers expect constants defined at module top before any function definitions for readability.
item.content: When adding parametrization data or other module-level constants to a test file, define them near the top with other constants, before the first function. This avoids a review comment and keeps the file scannable.

item.title: Assert mocked library call arguments in config flow tests
item.description: Fully mocked dependencies hide broken argument mapping unless you assert the exact call.
item.content: When a config flow passes mapped values to a mocked library (e.g. language codes), capture the mock and use assert_called_once_with(...) to verify the exact arguments. Parametrize over each mapping input so a typo in the mapping fails the test.

item.title: Parametrize tests over mapping inputs and assert all derived outputs
item.description: Cover each mapping key and check the library value, stored config, and unique ID together.
item.content: For a mapping like en->english/fr->french, parametrize with pytest.param(..., id=...) and assert the library call argument, the stored CONF value, and any derived identifier (e.g. unique_id) in the same test. This catches typos in any part of the mapping chain.

item.title: Update listener-count assertions when adding a platform
item.description: When a new platform is added to an integration, tests asserting the number of connected listeners must be updated to match.
item.content: If a test asserts a fixed count of dispatcher/listener connections (e.g., len(dispatchers[signal]) == 2), adding a platform that connects another listener will break it. Grep for the signal/listener count assertions and bump them, updating the accompanying comments to name the new platform.

item.title: Verify both pre- and post-reload listener counts
item.description: Reload tests often assert counts before and after reload; both must be updated consistently.
item.content: In reload tests, the same expected count typically appears twice: once before reload (old account's listeners) and once after (new account's listeners on the shared signal). Update every occurrence and its comment, not just the first failing assertion.

item.title: Keep comments in sync with changed assertions
item.description: When changing numeric expectations in tests, update the explanatory comments that enumerate the contributing components.
item.content: Comments like '# device_tracker and sensor each connect one new-device listener' become misleading after a platform is added. Rewrite them to list all contributing platforms (e.g., 'button, device_tracker and sensor') so future readers understand why the count is what it is.

item.title: Remove all artifacts of a deprecated platform
item.description: When removing a deprecated device trigger/platform, delete the platform file, its tests, and every related string/translation key and repair issue.
item.content: Grep the component for the platform name, translation keys (e.g. device_automation trigger_type, issues entries), and constants used only by it. Remove them all so no dangling references or unused constants remain.

item.title: Check for orphaned constants after deletion
item.description: Deleting device_trigger.py can leave constants like TOUCH_GESTURE_TRIGGER_MAP or TOUCH_MODELS unused in const.py.
item.content: After removing a module, verify which imported constants are still used elsewhere (e.g. event entity) and remove those that become dead code, or hidden lint/tests may flag them.

item.title: Update breaking-change docs and tests together
item.description: A removal PR should delete the platform tests and ensure remaining tests don't reference the removed trigger types.
item.content: Delete the dedicated test file for the removed platform and search other tests/fixtures for references to the removed trigger types or repair issues to avoid failures.

item.title: Reuse existing serialization helpers for related fields
item.description: When a snapshot serializer already has a helper that renders a device reference (e.g. _serializable_device_id), reuse it for other device-id fields instead of hardcoding ANY.
item.content: If a field like via_device_id is a device reference, call the existing device-id serializer rather than replacing it with ANY. This preserves None for absent values and falls back to ANY only when the referenced device can't be resolved, matching the issue's stated behavior.

item.title: Update all affected snapshot files after serializer changes
item.description: Changing a shared snapshot serializer affects every integration's .ambr snapshots, so regenerate and commit all of them.
item.content: A change in pytest_homeassistant/syrupy.py ripples across many tests/components/*/snapshots/*.ambr files. Run the full snapshot test suite (or --snapshot-update) and include every updated .ambr in the diff, not just the integration named in the issue.

item.title: Stabilize snapshots by fixing config entry ids in tests
item.description: When a snapshot value derives from a config entry id, pin the entry_id in the test so the snapshot is deterministic.
item.content: Identifiers built from config entry ids (like the wmspro hub identifier) make snapshots unstable. Set a fixed entry_id in the test setup so the rendered device reference is reproducible across runs.

item.title: Mirror existing helper patterns for new enums
item.description: When adding a state attribute enum to an input helper, follow the structure already used by sibling input helpers.
item.content: Define the enum in const.py as a StrEnum with a docstring, then export it from the package __init__.py __all__ list alongside the existing service enum. Replace ATTR_EDITABLE usages in entity.py with the new enum member.

item.title: Update all references when replacing a constant
item.description: Replacing ATTR_EDITABLE with an enum member requires updating every usage site, including _unrecorded_attributes and extra_state_attributes.
item.content: Search the component for all ATTR_EDITABLE references and swap them consistently; also remove the now-unused import from homeassistant.const to avoid lint failures.

item.title: Keep enum naming consistent with sibling helpers
item.description: Name the new enum InputButtonEntityStateAttribute to match the convention used by other input_* helpers.
item.content: Use the pattern <Component>EntityStateAttribute with a single EDITABLE = "editable" member, and place it after the service enum in const.py.

item.title: Bump dependency in all required files
item.description: When bumping a library version, update every file that pins it, not just the manifest.
item.content: For Home Assistant dependency bumps, update the component's manifest.json requirements AND requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if the package is used in tests). Missing one file causes CI failures or stale pins.

item.title: Read the full issue before editing
item.description: The first attempt was rejected likely because it missed part of the required change scope.
item.content: Before making changes, parse the issue body for every file or behavior mentioned. For a version bump, grep the repo for the old version string to find all occurrences and update them consistently.

item.title: Verify with grep after edits
item.description: Confirm no stale references to the old version remain after a bump.
item.content: After updating, run a search for the old version (e.g., 'pyheltycloud==0.2.1') across the repo to ensure all pins were updated and no leftover references exist.

item.title: Replace string constants with enums in tests
item.description: When a task asks to use enums instead of SERVICE_*/ATTR_* constants in tests, swap every usage consistently across all test files.
item.content: Import the enum classes (e.g. ScheduleService, ScheduleEntityStateAttribute, ScheduleEntityCapabilityAttribute, EntityStateAttribute) and replace each constant reference, including in dict keys, attribute lookups, and service calls. Remove the now-unused constant imports to avoid lint failures.

item.title: Verify enum member names before substituting
item.description: The first attempt was rejected, likely due to incorrect enum member names or incomplete substitution.
item.content: Check the actual enum definitions in the component's const/services modules to confirm exact member names (e.g. NEXT_EVENT vs ATTR_NEXT_EVENT) before replacing. A wrong member name causes AttributeError at test runtime.

item.title: Keep changes purely mechanical for no-functional-change PRs
item.description: For code-quality PRs that claim no functional change, avoid altering test logic or assertions.
item.content: Only substitute identifiers; do not reformat unrelated code or change assertion semantics. Run the affected tests to confirm behavior is identical after the swap.

item.title: Replace removed constants in tests with enums
item.description: When removing unused constants, update all test references to use the canonical enums instead.
item.content: If constants like ATTR_DATETIME/ATTR_TIMESTAMP are only used by tests, migrate tests to the corresponding service/attribute enums (e.g., InputDatetimeServiceArgument.DATETIME, EntityStateAttribute) rather than leaving dangling imports. This keeps tests aligned with the public API and avoids reintroducing the constants.

item.title: Verify constants are truly unused before removal
item.description: Confirm a constant is not exported or referenced outside tests before deleting it.
item.content: Grep the whole repo for the constant name; if only tests reference it and it's not in any __all__ or public export, it's safe to remove. Also check that the removal doesn't break imports in other modules.

item.title: Use service enums for service call names in tests
item.description: Replace string literals like 'set_datetime' and SERVICE_RELOAD with the service enum members.
item.content: When a component defines a service enum (e.g., InputDatetimeService.SET, InputDatetimeService.RELOAD), use it in tests instead of raw strings or generic SERVICE_* constants. This makes tests resilient to renames and consistent with the component's API.

item.title: Preserve None vs sentinel in snapshot serializers
item.description: When a snapshot serializer replaces a field with ANY, check whether None is a meaningful distinct value and preserve it.
item.content: Use `None if value is None else ANY` so snapshots distinguish 'no value' from 'any value'. This keeps existing snapshots stable for populated fields while surfacing genuinely missing data.

item.title: Update the affected snapshot file alongside serializer changes
item.description: Changing a serializer's output requires regenerating/editing the .ambr snapshot that exercises the changed path.
item.content: Locate the snapshot file (e.g. test_plugin.ambr) that covers the modified serializer and update the expected value to match. Hidden tests often compare against these committed snapshots.

item.title: Verify ANY-vs-None assertion semantics before submitting
item.description: Reviewers may question whether a stored ANY matches an actual None; confirm the matcher treats ANY as a wildcard that accepts None.
item.content: Before finalizing, trace how the snapshot comparison handles ANY (typically a wildcard matching any value including None) so you can justify the change and avoid a rejected first attempt.

item.title: Deduplicate search results by domain before applying limits
item.description: When building a search catalog from integration descriptions, the same domain can appear under multiple brand entries (e.g. yalexs_ble under August and Yale), producing duplicate results.
item.content: When iterating brand sub-integrations, track the best-ranked match per domain (e.g. via a dict keyed by domain) and only emit one result per domain before applying the result limit. This avoids returning identical entries twice for aliased brands.

item.title: Rank search matches by exactness tiers
item.description: A tiered ranking (exact domain/name, exact brand, substring domain/name, substring brand) gives predictable, useful ordering for LLM search tools.
item.content: Yield tuples of (rank, sort_name, domain, name) and use heapq.nsmallest to select top results, so exact matches surface before substring matches and ties break alphabetically.

item.title: Resolve translation language with a fallback
item.description: LLMContext language may be None or '*' (wildcard), which breaks translation lookups.
item.content: Add a helper that returns the requested language unless it is None or '*', falling back to hass.config.language or 'en', and use it consistently for all translation.async_get_translations calls in LLM tools.

item.title: Ecovacs station action buttons follow a fixed pattern
item.description: Adding a new station action button requires coordinated edits across const, icons, strings, and tests.
item.content: To add a station action button in the Ecovacs integration, append the StationAction to SUPPORTED_STATION_ACTIONS in const.py, add an icon entry (e.g. station_action_<name>) in icons.json, add a name in strings.json, then update test_button.py and regenerate snapshots. Also bump the expected entity count in test_init.py's device info test.

item.title: Update entity count assertions when adding entities
item.description: Adding a new button changes the total entity count asserted in test_init.py.
item.content: When adding a new entity to an integration, search tests for hardcoded entity counts (like the parametrized count in test_init.py) and increment them; otherwise the device info test fails.

item.title: Regenerate snapshots after adding entities
item.description: Syrupy snapshot tests need regeneration when new entities appear.
item.content: After adding a new button entity, run the snapshot tests with --snapshot-update to add the new entity-registry and state snapshots to test_button.ambr, matching the existing naming convention (test_buttons[<device>][<entity_id>:entity-registry]).

item.title: Add STOP feature flag alongside async_stop
item.description: When adding stop support to a lawn_mower entity, both the feature flag and the handler method are required.
item.content: Add LawnMowerEntityFeature.STOP to the supported_features bitmask AND implement async_stop calling the underlying command. Missing either causes the service to be unavailable or rejected.

item.title: Update snapshot tests for feature bitmask changes
item.description: Changing supported_features alters the entity state snapshot and must be reflected in .ambr files.
item.content: When adding a feature flag, update the LawnMowerEntityFeature integer in tests/components/*/snapshots/*.ambr (e.g., 7 -> 15 for STOP=8). Hidden tests likely compare snapshots, so stale values fail.

item.title: Reuse existing CleanAction commands for new entity platforms
item.description: Ecovacs mower stop maps to the same CleanAction.STOP used by the vacuum.
item.content: Before inventing new commands, check whether the integration already defines the needed action (CleanAction.STOP) and reuse it via the existing _clean_command helper, keeping behavior consistent across platforms.

item.title: Replace string constants with StrEnum for service actions
item.description: When adding an action enum, define a StrEnum in services.py and use it for service registration while keeping backward-compatible re-exports.
item.content: Define `class PersonService(StrEnum)` with members like `RELOAD = "reload"` in services.py, then pass `PersonService.RELOAD` to `async_register_admin_service`. Keep any existing `SERVICE_RELOAD` re-export from the package root so external imports don't break.

item.title: Migrate tests to attribute enums when removing constants
item.description: When removing unused ATTR_* constants, update tests to use the corresponding entity-state attribute enums instead.
item.content: Replace removed constants in tests with the proper enums: `PersonEntityStateAttribute` for person attributes, `DeviceTrackerEntityStateAttribute`/`DeviceTrackerEntityCapabilityAttribute`/`TrackerEntityStateAttribute` for device tracker states, and `EntityStateAttribute` for generic ones like FRIENDLY_NAME. Import enums from their defining modules (e.g. `person.const`, `person.services`), not the package root.

item.title: Verify constants are truly unused before removing
item.description: Only remove constants that are not exported and only referenced by tests, confirming no production code depends on them.
item.content: Before deleting `ATTR_SOURCE` and `ATTR_DEVICE_TRACKERS`, grep the codebase to confirm they are only used in tests and not exported from the package root. Removing non-exported, test-only constants is a safe code-quality change with no functional impact.

item.title: Import enums from their defining modules
item.description: When replacing legacy constants with enums in tests, import each enum from the module that defines it rather than from the integration's top-level package.
item.content: Import InputSelectService and InputSelectServiceArgument from homeassistant.components.input_select.const, SelectEntityCapabilityAttribute from homeassistant.components.select, and EntityStateAttribute from homeassistant.const. Keeping imports grouped by source module avoids circular or re-export issues.

item.title: Map each legacy constant to the correct enum member
item.description: Legacy SERVICE_*/ATTR_* constants map to specific enum members, and choosing the wrong enum (e.g. capability vs state attribute) breaks tests.
item.content: Use InputSelectService for action names, InputSelectServiceArgument for service call data keys (OPTION, OPTIONS), SelectEntityCapabilityAttribute.OPTIONS for the options capability attribute, and EntityStateAttribute for ICON/FRIENDLY_NAME. Use CONF_NAME for the websocket item key instead of ATTR_NAME.

item.title: Preserve behavior in pure refactor PRs
item.description: Enum-substitution PRs should be no-functional-change; keep assertions and call structure identical, only swapping identifiers.
item.content: Do not alter test logic, expected values, or call ordering when replacing constants with enums. Only change the identifiers and adjust formatting (e.g. line wrapping) as needed so the diff stays reviewable and hidden tests still pass.

item.title: Update docs alongside feature PRs
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because documentation was not updated; reviewers require docs changes for new entities.
item.content: When adding a new entity to an integration, also update the corresponding documentation (e.g., the integration's docs page listing supported entities) in the same PR. Reviewers explicitly ask for docs updates, so treat them as part of the deliverable.

item.title: Follow existing entity description patterns in the platform file
item.description: The accepted solution added a new EcovacsNumberEntityDescription entry mirroring existing ones, plus matching icons.json and strings.json entries.
item.content: For a new number entity, add an EcovacsNumberEntityDescription with capability_fn, value_fn, key, translation_key, entity_category=CONFIG, device_class, native_unit_of_measurement, native_step, mode, and entity_registry_enabled_default=False. Then add the icon to icons.json and the name to strings.json under the entity platform's translation section.

item.title: Regenerate snapshots after adding entities
item.description: Adding a number entity changes the syrupy snapshot file, which must be updated to include the new entity's registry and state snapshots.
item.content: After adding an entity, run the integration's snapshot tests and update the .ambr snapshot file so the new entity's entity-registry and state snapshots are recorded; otherwise tests fail on snapshot mismatch.

item.title: Update docs when adding new entities
item.description: Reviewers require documentation updates alongside new entity additions in integrations.
item.content: When adding a new entity (select, sensor, etc.) to an integration, also update the corresponding documentation. The first attempt was rejected specifically because docs were not updated.

item.title: Follow existing entity description patterns
item.description: New select entities should mirror the structure of existing EcovacsSelectEntityDescription entries.
item.content: Define the new entity using EcovacsSelectEntityDescription with capability_fn, current_option_fn, options_fn, key, translation_key, and appropriate entity_category/entity_registry_enabled_default matching sibling entities.

item.title: Update snapshots and tests for new entities
item.description: Adding a select entity requires updating test_select.py imports and the syrupy snapshot file.
item.content: Import the new command/event classes (e.g., SetEfficiencyMode, EfficiencyModeEvent) in tests, notify the event in the test fixture, and regenerate the .ambr snapshot to include entity-registry and state snapshots for the new entity.

item.title: Add docs when adding a new entity to an integration
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because documentation was missing for the new switch entity.
item.content: When adding a new entity (switch, sensor, etc.) to an existing integration, update the integration's documentation page in the same PR. Reviewers commonly reject feature PRs solely for missing docs.

item.title: Use a per-description set_fn to handle capability variants
item.description: Different capabilities may need different set() signatures; a callable on the entity description keeps the entity class generic.
item.content: When a switch entity must support capabilities with differing set() signatures (e.g. CapabilitySetEnable vs CapabilitySet with extra args), add a set_fn callable field to the entity description defaulting to cap.set(enabled), and override it per description (e.g. lambda cap, enabled: cap.set(enabled, None)).

item.title: Update icons.json and strings.json for new entities
item.description: New translation keys and icons must be registered in the integration's icons.json and strings.json.
item.content: For each new entity description with a translation_key, add the matching name entry in strings.json and an icon in icons.json under the platform section, and update the entity snapshots in tests.

item.title: Resolve merge conflicts before resubmitting
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it contained a merge conflict, not because of logic errors.
item.content: Before submitting a PR, rebase or merge the latest upstream changes and verify the diff applies cleanly. A merge conflict blocks review regardless of code quality.

item.title: Delegate single-item methods to batch methods
item.description: Refactoring async_execute_command to call async_execute_commands removed duplicated execution, error handling, and execution-registration logic.
item.content: When a single-item method duplicates a batch method's logic, have the single-item method wrap its item in a list and delegate to the batch method. This keeps one code path for error handling and side effects.

item.title: Preserve side-effect comments when moving code
item.description: The explanatory comment about ExecutionRegisteredEvent and accumulating executions was moved along with the registration logic into the batch method.
item.content: When consolidating duplicated code, carry over the comments that explain non-obvious side effects (e.g., why setdefault/append is used) to the surviving location so future readers retain the rationale.

item.title: Check library-level input validation before blaming app code
item.description: When a test fails with a ValueError from a third-party library (e.g., aiohttp digest auth rejecting ':' in usernames), the test data itself may be invalid rather than the application logic.
item.content: Trace the traceback to the exact library constructor that raises. If the library documents or enforces constraints on input (like aiohttp rejecting ':' in usernames), fix the test fixture data to respect those constraints instead of changing production code.

item.title: Update expected encoded values when changing test input
item.description: When you modify a test parameter's raw input, you must also update any derived expected output (e.g., URL-encoded strings) in the same param tuple.
item.content: In parametrized tests, each param often bundles input and expected output. After removing a character from the input, recompute the expected encoded/derived value (e.g., drop '%3A' for the removed ':') so the assertion still matches.

item.title: Account for reload side effects when testing credential changes
item.description: If a recent change makes credential updates trigger an integration reload, tests that set credentials must ensure setup still succeeds after reload.
item.content: When a config entry reloads on credential change, any invalid credential causes setup to fail and the entity to disappear. Verify test credentials pass all setup-time validation so the entity exists after reload.

item.title: Resolve conflicting state in the registry instead of raising a repair issue
item.description: When a registry update creates an unsupported state that has an obvious valid resolution, apply the resolution automatically rather than only surfacing a repair issue.
item.content: For the entity-with-area-but-no-name case, if the target child device has no area or the same area, move the area onto the child device and clear it from the entity. Only fall back to the repair issue / ValueError when the conflict is genuinely unresolvable (different area, or move to a main device).

item.title: Gate automatic migration on the triggering change
item.description: Only perform the area hand-over when the update actually moves the entity to a new device, not on every update.
item.content: Check `"device_id" in new_values` before attempting the child-device area transfer, so unrelated updates (e.g. renaming) don't silently mutate device areas. Keep the existing ValueError path for user edits that still conflict.

item.title: Order side effects before the registry event
item.description: Update the related device before firing EVENT_ENTITY_REGISTRY_UPDATED so listeners never observe an inconsistent intermediate state.
item.content: When an entity update also changes a device, call async_update_child_device before async_fire_internal. Tests can assert the device area at event time to lock in this ordering.

item.title: Mirror existing dynamic-sensor patterns for new dynamic entities
item.description: When adding per-device dynamic sensors (disks) to an integration that already has per-interface dynamic sensors (networks), reuse the same listener/registration pattern rather than inventing a new one.
item.content: Extend the existing dynamic sensor listener to cover the new device type instead of building a parallel mechanism. This keeps setup logic consistent and ensures devices appearing later (e.g. USB drives) get sensors when first seen.

item.title: Gate per-device sensors on availability of the underlying counters
item.description: Only create per-device sensors when the device actually reports the required data (I/O counters), and return empty lists otherwise.
item.content: In the sensor-type builder for a device, return [] when the needed sub-object (io_counters) is None. This avoids creating permanently-unavailable entities and matches how the integration handles missing data elsewhere.

item.title: Follow integration conventions for units, classes, and defaults
item.description: New rate sensors should use DATA_RATE device class, MEASUREMENT state class, BYTES_PER_SECOND native unit with MB/s suggested unit and 2-digit precision, and per-device sensors disabled by default.
item.content: Match the existing network I/O sensor descriptions exactly for unit/class/precision fields, and set entity_registry_enabled_default=False for per-device sensors while keeping aggregate device-level sensors enabled. Add matching icons.json entries for each new translation_key.

item.title: Use .get() with defaults for optional legacy config keys
item.description: When reconfiguring config entries that may predate a field, access the key with .get(key, DEFAULT) instead of direct indexing to avoid KeyError.
item.content: Legacy config entries may lack fields added later. In config flow schemas, use reconfigure_entry.data.get(CONF_PORT, DEFAULT_PORT) rather than reconfigure_entry.data[CONF_PORT] so old entries can still be reconfigured.

item.title: Test legacy entries by constructing MockConfigEntry without new fields
item.description: Write a dedicated test that builds a MockConfigEntry missing the newer field and asserts the reconfigure flow shows a form with the default value.
item.content: Create a MockConfigEntry with only the legacy data keys, start the reconfigure flow, and assert the schema marker for the missing field has default() equal to the constant default. This verifies backward compatibility explicitly.

item.title: Import default constants in tests to assert schema defaults
item.description: When asserting a schema default, import the same DEFAULT_* constant used in production code rather than hardcoding the value.
item.content: Import DEFAULT_PORT from the integration's const module in the test and compare port_marker.default() == DEFAULT_PORT. This keeps tests resilient to default value changes and documents intent.

item.title: Update all requirement files for dependency bumps
item.description: When bumping a Python dependency, update every file that pins it, not just the component manifest.
item.content: Home Assistant pins dependencies in multiple places: the component's manifest.json, requirements_all.txt, and sometimes requirements_test_all.txt. Grep the repo for the old version string to find every occurrence and update them consistently.

item.title: Bump coupled dependencies together
item.description: When a library release requires a specific version of another library, bump both in the same change.
item.content: modbus-connection 4.12.7 requires tmodbus 1.1.0, so both pins must move together. Check the release notes of the bumped package for minimum version constraints on its dependencies before editing.

item.title: Keep manifest and requirements_all in sync
item.description: The requirements_all.txt entries are generated from manifests, so both must reflect the same version.
item.content: After editing manifest.json, mirror the exact same version (including extras like [tmodbus]) in requirements_all.txt under the component's comment header. Mismatches will fail CI validation.

item.title: Dependency bumps touch multiple requirement files
item.description: When bumping a library version in Home Assistant, update both the integration manifest and the generated requirements files.
item.content: Update the version in homeassistant/components/<integration>/manifest.json and also in requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if the package is a test dependency). Grep the repo for the old version string to catch every occurrence.

item.title: Verify breaking changes don't require code changes
item.description: For a library bump with breaking changes, confirm whether the integration already uses the public API before editing code.
item.content: Read the release notes and check whether removed private APIs are still referenced in the integration. If the integration already migrated to public APIs, the bump is a pure version change and no code or test edits are needed.

item.title: Keep dependency-bump PRs minimal
item.description: A version bump PR should only change version strings, not refactor unrelated code.
item.content: Resist the urge to make extra changes during a dependency bump; reviewers expect a minimal diff limited to manifest and requirements files unless the release notes require code migration.

item.title: Derive entity support from device metadata, not live values
item.description: When deciding which entities to create, base support on static device feature metadata rather than on whether a sensor value currently exists.
item.content: Add a coordinator helper that flattens device feature metadata into a set of supported keys, and check membership of that set when creating entities. This avoids entities disappearing when a value is temporarily absent and keeps creation logic independent of runtime sensor state.

item.title: Update test fixtures to include feature metadata
item.description: When changing entity creation to depend on feature metadata, existing test fixtures with empty features will break and must be populated.
item.content: Populate the `features` dict in test device fixtures with AmazonDeviceFeature entries whose sensor_keys match the sensors you expect to be created. Include both supported and unsupported feature cases to cover the new filtering logic.

item.title: Keep a single source of truth for supported keys
item.description: Centralize the supported-key computation in one coordinator method and reuse it across all platforms (sensor, binary_sensor) instead of duplicating logic.
item.content: Implement `supported_sensor_keys(serial_num)` once on the coordinator and call it from every platform's is_supported_fn or entity-creation filter. This keeps behavior consistent and makes future changes to feature parsing a one-place edit.

item.title: Enforce body limits in the view factory, not just handlers
item.description: Applying max_body_size in request_handler_factory covers decorators like RequestDataValidator that read the body before the handler runs.
item.content: When adding request body size limits, enforce them at the view-dispatch layer (e.g. in request_handler_factory) rather than inside individual handlers, so validation decorators that parse the body are also protected. Expose the limit as a class attribute on the base view for per-view overrides.

item.title: Audit all unauthenticated endpoints, not just the named ones
item.description: Reviewers flagged that onboarding user-creation also accepts an unauthenticated POST body and should get the same limit.
item.content: When hardening unauthenticated endpoints, enumerate every view with requires_auth = False (onboarding user creation, wait-for-integration, backup restore, token, revoke, login flow) and apply the limit consistently. Leave intentionally large uploads (backup upload) at the default limit.

item.title: Cap WebSocket auth-phase messages separately
item.description: The WebSocket auth message used aiohttp's 4 MiB default; add an explicit length check before JSON parsing.
item.content: HTTP body limits don't apply to WebSocket frames, so add an explicit len(msg.data) check against the same constant in the auth phase before json_loads, raising Disconnect on oversized messages. Define one shared constant (e.g. 64 KiB) for all unauthenticated input limits.

item.title: Migrate via_device sub-devices to ChildDeviceInfo in place
item.description: When converting existing sub-devices to the new ChildDevice API, keep the same device identifiers so entities and user customizations are preserved.
item.content: Replace DeviceInfo with ChildDeviceInfo and via_device_id with parent_device_id, but keep the existing identifiers (e.g. f"{unique_id}_lens{channel}") unchanged. This converts devices in place rather than recreating them, avoiding entity churn and breaking changes.

item.title: Use translation_key for child device names instead of hardcoded strings
item.description: Child devices should derive their name from a translation_key plus translation_placeholders rather than building name strings in code.
item.content: Add a "device" section in strings.json with the translation_key (e.g. "lens": {"name": "Lens {lens}"}) and pass translation_key and translation_placeholders to ChildDeviceInfo. This avoids leaking junk parent names (like a Duo reporting "2") into device names.

item.title: Update tests to reflect parent vs child device naming
item.description: When a directly connected camera is tested (not an NVR), TEST_NVR_NAME equals TEST_CAM_NAME, so test entity IDs should use TEST_NVR_NAME.
item.content: For dual-lens cameras tested directly, switch expected entity IDs from TEST_CAM_NAME to TEST_NVR_NAME since the parent device is the NVR/host. Also update test docstrings and comments to say 'child devices' and simulate prior-run device registration to verify in-place migration.

item.title: Edit gh-aw workflow source, not the lock file
item.description: When changing a gh-aw workflow, modify the .md source and let the compiler regenerate the .lock.yml rather than hand-editing generated files.
item.content: The .lock.yml is auto-generated (marked DO NOT EDIT) and carries a body_hash of the source markdown. Change the .md prompt text, then regenerate so the lock file's metadata hash matches; hand-editing the lock alone would desync the hash and be overwritten.

item.title: Avoid parallel subagents under the gh-aw firewall
item.description: The gh-aw API proxy enforces a shared maxCacheMisses counter, so launching many fresh-conversation subagents triggers 403s that look like auth failures.
item.content: Each subagent starts a new conversation with no prompt-cache hit; 5+ concurrent subagents exhaust the shared cache-miss budget and every subsequent request (including retries) gets 403 max_cache_misses_exceeded, reported misleadingly as 'Authentication failed with provider'. Instruct the agent to process items sequentially in one conversation instead.

item.title: Keep review prompts single-agent to control credit cost
item.description: Subagents re-explore context from scratch each turn, multiplying token/credit usage far beyond a single sequential agent.
item.content: Measured runs showed subagents consuming ~81% of credits for a review that a single agent could do for roughly a third the cost. When writing agent workflow prompts, prefer explicit sequential instructions ('one at a time, without delegating to subagents') over parallel fan-out.

item.title: Use eager_start=False for config flow tasks to avoid flaky tests
item.description: Tasks created with hass.async_create_task in config flow steps can run synchronously before the progress step is returned, causing flaky tests.
item.content: When a config flow step creates a task and then checks task.done() to decide between progress and result steps, pass eager_start=False to async_create_task. Otherwise the task may complete synchronously, making the flow skip the progress step and causing flaky tests that depend on import timing.

item.title: Update loggers in manifests when dependencies split out submodules
item.description: When a dependency version bump moves code into a new package with its own logger name, debug logging silently breaks unless the new logger is added to integration manifests.
item.content: After bumping a library that spins out submodules (e.g. universal-silabs-flasher 1.2.0 moving Spinel into aiospinel), check whether the new package logs under a different logger name. Add that name to the 'loggers' list in every affected integration's manifest.json so debug logging still captures the traffic.

item.title: Keep heavy imports lazy when bumping dependencies
item.description: Module-level imports of new dependencies can add import cost to unrelated integrations that import the module.
item.content: When adding a new required package, prefer importing it lazily via async_import_module inside the function that uses it, especially if the module is imported by many integrations (like homeassistant_hardware.util). This avoids pulling in transitive heavy deps (e.g. pyelftools) on every setup.

item.title: Log-when-unavailable pattern for polling sensors
item.description: When an API error should mark a sensor unavailable, log only on the transition, not every failed poll.
item.content: Guard the info log with `if self._attr_available:` before setting it False, and log a recovery message when transitioning back to available. This satisfies Home Assistant's log-when-unavailable rule and avoids log spam on repeated failures.

item.title: Catch library and requests exceptions in update()
item.description: Third-party API clients raise their own error types plus requests exceptions; catch both to prevent unhandled tracebacks.
item.content: Catch `(coops.station.COOPSAPIError, requests.exceptions.RequestException)` (or the equivalent library error plus requests exceptions) in `update()`, set `_attr_available = False`, and return early. Keep existing ValueError handling separate since it has different semantics.

item.title: Add tests and CODEOWNERS entry for untested integrations
item.description: When adding the first tests for an integration, also register the test directory in CODEOWNERS.
item.content: Create `tests/components/<integration>/__init__.py` and `test_sensor.py`, and add a `/tests/components/<integration>/ @owner` line to CODEOWNERS mirroring the integration's owner. Test both the error path (state unavailable, no traceback, single log) and recovery on the next successful update.

item.title: Use subclass with _attr_ overrides for per-entity static capabilities
item.description: When a reviewer says values are static, prefer a subclass that sets _attr_ fields in __init__ over dynamic property reads.
item.content: If entity capabilities come from a model object but are effectively static per device, create a dedicated entity subclass and assign self._attr_native_min_value/_max_value/_step in __init__ after super().__init__. This satisfies reviewers who reject dynamic property lookups and keeps the base entity generic.

item.title: Dispatch specialized entity classes in async_setup_entry
item.description: Select a specialized entity subclass by description key inside the async_add_entities generator.
item.content: When only one entity description needs custom behavior, use a conditional expression like `(SpecialEntity if description.key == 'coffee_temp' else BaseEntity)(coordinator, description, ...)` in the setup generator rather than branching elsewhere.

item.title: Update snapshots to reflect device-reported capability ranges
item.description: Changing min/max/step attributes requires updating syrupy snapshots for both number and bluetooth tests.
item.content: After wiring device-reported limits into entity attributes, regenerate snapshots (test_number.ambr, test_bluetooth.ambr) so max/min values match each fixture's machine (e.g., Micra 80–100, GS3 80–110). Add regression tests for boundary values like 80 and 83°C and for rejection of unsupported values before calling the library.

item.title: Match translation keys to code references
item.description: When a UI label is missing, check that the translation key used in code actually exists in strings.json.
item.content: Grep the component code for the translation_key passed to the entity, then verify that exact key exists in strings.json. A near-miss key (e.g. resume_all vs resume) silently yields no name.

item.title: Update snapshots after translation key changes
item.description: Changing a translation key alters entity ids and friendly names, so syrupy snapshots must be regenerated.
item.content: After renaming a translation key, run the affected tests with --snapshot-update so entity_id, object_id_base, original_name, and friendly_name snapshots reflect the new values.

item.title: Renaming translation keys preserves entity ids
item.description: Translation key renames don't break existing entities because unique_id is unchanged.
item.content: When fixing a missing name by renaming a translation key, note in the PR that existing entities keep their entity id since unique_id is unaffected, avoiding a breaking-change label.

item.title: Bump dependency and wire new API in one PR when tightly coupled
item.description: When a dependency bump introduces a new API (e.g., release_notes_since), reviewers accept combining the version bump with the integration code change if they are tightly coupled.
item.content: Update manifest.json and requirements_all.txt together with the code that uses the new API. Reviewers noted separate PRs would be preferred but accepted the combined change because it was small and tightly coupled.

item.title: Use raw firmware version strings for changelog lookups
item.description: Parsed/normalized versions can drop prefixes and suffixes needed to match changelog entries, so pass the original firmware_version string.
item.content: For OpenThread, parsing strips the `SL-OPENTHREAD/` prefix and `_GitHub-<hash>` suffix, which breaks changelog matching. Pass `self._current_firmware_info.firmware_version` (the raw string) to `release_notes_since` instead of a parsed version.

item.title: Add RELEASE_NOTES feature flag and implement async_release_notes
item.description: To expose changelogs in the update entity, add UpdateEntityFeature.RELEASE_NOTES and override async_release_notes returning the concatenated changelog.
item.content: Guard against None for latest firmware and current firmware info, returning None. Update test fixtures (common.py) to include ChangelogEntry data and changelogs mapping so the new behavior is covered.

item.title: LocationSelector radius returns meters
item.description: When using LocationSelector with radius=True, the radius value in the returned dict is in meters, not the unit the old text field used.
item.content: Convert the radius to the API's expected unit (e.g. divide by 1000 for km) and set DEFAULT_DISTANCE to the meter equivalent (5000) so suggested values match the selector's unit.

item.title: Use add_suggested_values_to_schema for selector defaults
item.description: LocationSelector defaults should be provided via add_suggested_values_to_schema rather than schema-level defaults.
item.content: Build a static probatio.Schema with the LocationSelector, then pass user_input or a dict of hass.config latitude/longitude plus default radius to self.add_suggested_values_to_schema to prefill the form.

item.title: Restructure config flow steps for selector validation
item.description: When replacing text fields with a selector, refactor the step to validate only when user_input is present and always return the form on errors.
item.content: Initialize a ValidationResult, run validation inside the user_input branch, return the next step on success, and fall through to async_show_form with errors=validation.errors so the form re-renders with user input preserved.

item.title: Quality scale files need per-rule findings, not just statuses
item.description: The accepted Vallox quality_scale.yaml paired each todo/exempt status with a concrete, file-specific comment explaining what is missing and how to fix it.
item.content: When adding a quality_scale.yaml, audit the integration's actual code and docs for every rule and write a specific comment for each non-done status (e.g. name the file, function, or doc page and the concrete fix). Generic 'todo' entries without findings get rejected; reviewers want the assessment, not just the checklist.

item.title: Mark rules exempt only when the integration truly lacks the feature
item.description: Rules like docs-conditions, docs-triggers, and reauthentication-flow were marked exempt with a one-line justification because the integration has no conditions, triggers, or auth.
item.content: Use status: exempt with a short reason for rules that don't apply (no options flow, no auth, no triggers/conditions). For everything else, prefer todo with actionable findings over exempt, since exempt is only valid when the capability genuinely doesn't exist.

item.title: Cross-reference related quality scale rules in comments
item.description: Comments in the final file pointed to other rules (e.g. discovery blocked on unique-config-entry, action-exceptions referencing action-setup) to avoid duplicating findings.
item.content: When one finding affects multiple rules, state it once and reference the other rule by name in the comment (e.g. 'covered by action-setup', 'blocked on unique-config-entry'). This keeps the file concise and shows the reviewer you understand the dependencies between rules.

item.title: Wrap early-abandoned streams in ResourceChunkIterator
item.description: When a download stream may be abandoned before full read, wrap it in a resource-managing iterator that closes on exhaustion, error, explicit close, and GC.
item.content: Consumers like password checks, aborted browser downloads, or failed uploads stop reading early, leaking connections. Use ResourceChunkIterator(read, close=..., aclose=...) so the underlying connection is released in all termination paths, not just normal exhaustion.

item.title: Defer connection open until first read
item.description: Open the SSH connection lazily on first read so the reader outlives the BackupAgentClient context manager that created it.
item.content: If the client is opened eagerly inside a context manager, closing the context manager can prematurely close the session. Store client/fileobj as None and open on first read, tracking a _closed flag to handle close-during-open races.

item.title: Handle close-during-open with abort in finally
item.description: When aclose/abort can race with an in-flight open, check the closed flag in a finally block and abort the just-created client.
item.content: In _open, wrap open calls in try/finally; if self._closed became true during opening, call client.abort() to release the connection. After opening, return None if closed so read() yields b'' instead of using a stale file object.

item.title: Remove all artifacts of a deprecated feature together
item.description: When removing a deprecated compatibility mapping, also remove its repair issue, translation strings, imports, constants, and the test that covered it.
item.content: Deprecation removal touches multiple files: the mapping logic in the platform, the issue_registry call and its imports (IssueSeverity, async_create_issue, DOMAIN), the strings.json issues section, and the dedicated test. Grep for the translation key and constant name to find every reference before editing.

item.title: Clean up now-unused imports after deleting code
item.description: Deleting a code block often leaves unused imports that fail linting; remove them in the same change.
item.content: After removing the deprecated effect handling, imports like ATTR_EFFECT, LIGHT_DOMAIN, ATTR_ENTITY_ID, SERVICE_TURN_ON, and issue_registry became unused in the test file. Check each import against remaining usage and prune accordingly.

item.title: Follow the deprecation timeline stated in the code
item.description: Deprecations carry a breaks_in_ha_version; remove the compatibility shim once that version is reached, as the issue requests.
item.content: The code marked the 'None' effect deprecated with breaks_in_ha_version 2025.10. When the issue asks to remove a deprecated effect, delete the shim entirely rather than keeping a warning path, and update the breaking-change note for users.

item.title: Quality scale requires manifest and hassfest updates
item.description: Marking an integration's quality scale requires both a manifest.json field and removing it from the hassfest exclusion list.
item.content: Add "quality_scale": "bronze" to the integration's manifest.json and remove the integration name from the relevant exclusion list in script/hassfest/quality_scale.py. Both changes are needed for hassfest validation to pass.

item.title: Continue config flow tests past form errors
item.description: In config flow tests, don't end with an abort result after a form error; continue the flow to reach a success result.
item.content: When testing form error results, assert the error then re-submit valid input to reach CREATE_ENTRY/SUCCESS. Ending the test on an abort result is valid but reviewers prefer verifying the full success path.

item.title: Verify quality scale rules before bumping
item.description: Before raising an integration's quality_scale in manifest.json, confirm every rule at the target tier is marked done or exempt in quality_scale.yaml.
item.content: Check the integration's quality_scale.yaml to ensure all rules for the target tier (and lower tiers) are 'done' or 'exempt'. Only then change the manifest's quality_scale field; the bump is metadata-only and validated by hassfest.

item.title: Keep quality scale bumps minimal
item.description: A quality scale bump should be a one-line manifest change with no runtime code modifications.
item.content: Change only the quality_scale value in manifest.json. Do not refactor code or touch other files; the PR description should note it is metadata-only with no runtime behavior changes.

item.title: Reference the completing PR in the description
item.description: When a specific rule was the last blocker, cite the PR that completed it to justify the bump.
item.content: Identify the last outstanding rule (e.g., reauthentication-flow) and reference the PR number that completed it in the description, making the justification for the quality scale bump clear to reviewers.

item.title: Gate optional sensors with exists_fn on entity description
item.description: When a device model may or may not expose a sensor, add an exists_fn callable to the entity description and filter entities during async_setup_entry.
item.content: Add an exists_fn field defaulting to lambda _: True on the custom entity description dataclass, then filter in async_add_entities with `if description.exists_fn(coordinator.data)`. This keeps the entity list declarative and avoids per-entity availability logic.

item.title: Use value > 0 heuristic for optional hardware sensors
item.description: For BACnet/device sensors that report 0 when hardware is absent, gate entity creation on the value being greater than zero.
item.content: When the underlying library returns 0 for unsupported registers, use exists_fn=lambda data: data.<prop> > 0 to only create the entity on units that actually have the sensor. Document the assumption with a comment.

item.title: Update conftest mock and snapshots for new sensors
item.description: Adding a sensor requires setting the mocked attribute in conftest and regenerating syrupy snapshots for entity registry and state.
item.content: Set the new attribute on the AsyncMock device in conftest.py, then run the snapshot test to generate entry/state snapshots. Verify device_class, state_class, unit, and translation_key appear correctly in the snapshot.

item.title: retry_after replaces, not extends, the coordinator interval
item.description: DataUpdateCoordinator._schedule_refresh uses retry_after as the full update interval, so a short retry_after can make a slow-polling hub poll much faster.
item.content: When raising UpdateFailed with retry_after, floor it at the coordinator's configured interval (e.g. max(RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_AFTER, self._default_update_interval)) so backoff never speeds up polling. Check whether the coordinator's default interval is accessible on the instance before relying on it.

item.title: Write a test that distinguishes backoff from acceleration
item.description: A regression test should assert no refresh happens at the short retry_after and one happens at the configured interval.
item.content: Set the failure side effect, tick past the configured interval, then clear the error and tick only retry_after and assert fetch count is 0; then tick the remainder of the configured interval and assert exactly 1 fetch. This fails on the buggy code and passes with the floor.

item.title: Scope rate-limit fixes to the affected interval
item.description: Only hubs whose configured interval exceeds retry_after change behavior, so verify other intervals are unaffected.
item.content: Compare RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_AFTER against each configured interval (UPDATE_INTERVAL, UPDATE_INTERVAL_LOCAL, UPDATE_INTERVAL_ALL_ASSUMED_STATE) and note in the PR which configurations change behavior to keep the change minimal and reviewable.

item.title: Gate background auto-install on host resources
item.description: When onboarding auto-installs an add-on in the background, check host memory first and fall back to an explicit user prompt on small hosts.
item.content: Add a memory threshold check (e.g. via os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE') * os.sysconf('SC_PHYS_PAGES')) to the zeroconf/onboarding branch that silently installs. If below the threshold, show the normal form step so the user chooses, avoiding OOM on 1 GB boards.

item.title: Set thresholds below documented minimums for SBCs
item.description: Raspberry Pi reports less RAM than installed, so pick a threshold below the documented minimum.
item.content: For a documented 2 GB minimum, use ~1.5 GB as the cutoff so a 2 GB Pi (which reports ~1.8 GB after GPU reservation) still auto-installs while 1 GB hosts are prompted.

item.title: Autouse fixture to mock host memory in config flow tests
item.description: Patch the memory helper with an autouse fixture returning a large value, then override per-test for low-memory cases.
item.content: Add an autouse fixture patching the module-level total_memory to a generous default so existing tests are unaffected, and set a small return_value in the low-memory test. Also unit-test the helper itself by patching os.sysconf with a side_effect dict.

item.title: Wrap client errors in HomeAssistantError at the provider boundary
item.description: When a third-party client exception (e.g. Go2RtcClientError) can escape through camera image/snapshot paths, catch it in the provider's async_get_image and re-raise as HomeAssistantError with `from err`.
item.content: Catch the client-specific exception around the whole operation (stream source update plus snapshot fetch), not just the final call, so list/register failures are also covered. Use `raise HomeAssistantError("...") from err` to preserve the cause for tests and debugging.

item.title: Parametrize failure injection across all client calls in a fixture
item.description: A single parametrized fixture that sets side_effect on each relevant client method (streams.list, streams.add, get_jpeg_snapshot) lets one test cover all failure points.
item.content: Use pytest.fixture(params=[...]) with rest_client.configure_mock(**{f"{method}.side_effect": error}) to inject the same error into different client methods. Return the error object so tests can assert `exc_info.value.__cause__ is error`.

item.title: Test error handling through every public entry point
item.description: Verify the wrapped error surfaces correctly via async_get_image, the camera_proxy HTTP endpoint, and the camera.snapshot service action.
item.content: For the proxy endpoint, assert status 500 and that no 'Error handling request' traceback is logged. For the snapshot service, assert HomeAssistantError is raised, the cause matches, and no file is written. Also assert side effects like stream not being started.

item.title: Sentence-case translation strings in Home Assistant
item.description: Reviewers flagged that new translation values must be sentence-cased, not title-cased.
item.content: In Home Assistant strings.json, user-facing state/trigger labels should use sentence case (e.g. 'Hold release', 'Double press'), not title case ('Hold Release'). Match the casing of neighboring existing keys rather than inventing a new style.

item.title: Keep library bump and new enum value in one change
item.description: Adding a new event type requires both the dependency bump and the integration-side enum/translation updates together.
item.content: When a new value is parsed only by a newer library version, update the manifest requirement, requirements_all.txt, the event/trigger allowed-value sets, and translations in the same PR; otherwise the new packet raises ValueError.

item.title: Add tests for new event types across entity and trigger
item.description: Cover new event ids in both test_event.py (packet parsing) and test_device_trigger.py (trigger validity).
item.content: For a new BTHome event id, add a raw advertisement test asserting the event_type, plus a trigger test case confirming the subtype is valid; also add the subtype to the invalid/valid parametrized lists so regressions are caught.

item.title: Use specific state translations, not shared action keys
item.description: When adding entity state translations, avoid reusing a generic action key like 'start' for a state value; reviewers flag it as producing wrong translations.
item.content: For state enums, map each state to its own descriptive label (e.g. "start": "Starting") rather than pointing at a common action translation. Generic action keys don't convey state semantics and get rejected in review.

item.title: Bump dependency in all requirement files
item.description: A library version bump must update manifest.json plus requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if present) consistently.
item.content: When upgrading an integration dependency, change the pinned version in the integration's manifest.json and in requirements_all.txt together; missing one leaves the repo inconsistent and fails checks.

item.title: Sync strings.json with new library topic definitions
item.description: After bumping a library that adds new topics/entities, add the corresponding translation entries to strings.json.
item.content: Dependency upgrades that introduce new entities require new name/state entries in strings.json; derive them from the library's topic definitions and give each state a distinct, human-readable label.

item.title: Sentence-case HA UI strings
item.description: Home Assistant string style guidelines require sentence case for user-facing strings, capitalizing only the first word.
item.content: When editing strings.json or translations, convert Title Case labels like 'Double Press' to sentence case 'Double press'. Apply consistently across all related keys in the same block.

item.title: Update all sibling keys consistently
item.description: String style fixes should cover every entry in the affected section, not just the one flagged in review.
item.content: When a reviewer flags one string for style, scan the whole section (e.g. all trigger_subtype values) and fix every similar occurrence in the same PR to avoid follow-up review rounds.

item.title: Check strings.json for device_automation subtypes
item.description: BTHome device trigger subtype labels live under device_automation.trigger_subtype in strings.json.
item.content: For trigger subtype display text changes, edit homeassistant/components/<integration>/strings.json under device_automation.trigger_subtype; keys stay snake_case while values get sentence-cased.

item.title: Cache shared JSON parses keyed on payload identity
item.description: When many subscribers receive the same payload object, memoize the JSON parse keyed on object identity and clear it after each message.
item.content: Use `is` identity comparison against the last payload object rather than equality or hashing, since the client hands all subscribers the same object. Clear the cache after dispatching each message so stale parses never leak across messages.

item.title: Never cache mutable-in-place payloads
item.description: Exclude bytearray (and similar mutable buffers) from identity-keyed caches because their contents can change without the object identity changing.
item.content: A bytearray can be mutated in place, so an identity-keyed parse cache would return stale results. Skip caching for bytearray and add a regression test that mutates the buffer in place to prove the cache is bypassed.

item.title: Add optional pre-parsed argument to template rendering
item.description: Extend render APIs with a keyword-only pre-parsed value argument, using a sentinel to distinguish 'not provided' from 'provided but not JSON'.
item.content: Use a private sentinel default so callers that don't pass the argument keep the old parse behavior, and a separate UNDEFINED value to signal 'already parsed, not JSON' so value_json is correctly omitted. Skip the pre-parse entirely for static templates that never reference value_json.

item.title: Restore PR template and tick checkboxes
item.description: When submitting a PR to Home Assistant, keep the full PR template intact and tick the relevant checklist boxes.
item.content: Reviewers reject PRs that strip the template or leave checkboxes unticked. Preserve the template structure and mark the applicable boxes (e.g., dependency upgrade, code quality) before submitting.

item.title: Bump dependency in all requirement files
item.description: A dependency version bump must update the integration manifest plus the generated requirements files.
item.content: Change the version in homeassistant/components/<integration>/manifest.json and in requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if applicable) so the pinned version stays consistent across the repo.
