item.title: Keep stacked PRs scoped to their own change
item.description: When splitting a large change into stacked PRs, each PR's diff should contain only its own change.
item.content: For a dependency bump PR, only touch the version pins; leave coordinator/entity/sensor changes to their respective stacked PRs so reviewers can evaluate each part independently.

item.title: Update both CODEOWNERS and manifest.json for codeowner changes
item.description: Adding a codeowner to a Home Assistant integration requires editing two files, not just one.
item.content: When adding a codeowner, update both the integration's manifest.json `codeowners` array and the root CODEOWNERS file. Add entries for both the component directory and its tests directory (e.g., /homeassistant/components/X/ and /tests/components/X/).

item.title: Keep CODEOWNERS entries alphabetically ordered
item.description: CODEOWNERS in Home Assistant is sorted alphabetically by path, so insert new entries in the correct position.
item.content: Place new CODEOWNERS lines in alphabetical order relative to surrounding paths to match the existing file structure and avoid review friction.

item.title: Expect non-code review requests on trivial PRs
item.description: A first attempt was rejected with a request to message on Discord, not a code issue.
item.content: For small metadata PRs like codeowner additions, reviewers may ask for off-band communication (e.g., Discord) before merging; this is a process step, not a code defect, so don't over-engineer the diff in response.

item.title: Use primary_display_category for device-type filtering
item.description: Reviewers preferred filtering devices by primary_display_category over inspecting feature sets when deciding which platform entities to create.
item.content: When adding a new platform to an existing integration, gate entity creation on the device's primary display category (e.g. == 'LIGHT') rather than probing feature dictionaries. It is more robust and extensible as more devices are added.

item.title: Wrap API calls with the coordinator error handler
item.description: All feature-operation calls should go through the shared alexa_api_call context manager so errors are captured consistently.
item.content: Reviewers flagged a call path that bypassed the coordinator's error handling. Route every API invocation through the same helper (alexa_api_call(self.coordinator)) used elsewhere so CannotSetFeature and connection errors are translated uniformly.

item.title: Guard brightness scaling against 1% edge cases
item.description: Converting brightness with a (1,100) scale can yield 0 and break devices; verify and clamp the minimum.
item.content: When mapping HA brightness (0-255) to a device scale like 1-100, test the 1% case explicitly. Use brightness_to_value/value_to_brightness with the scale and ensure the result never rounds to 0 if the device rejects it; add a snapshot test covering minimum brightness.

item.title: Bulk-remove deprecated API calls across all integrations
item.description: When dropping an unused API like `_set_confirm_only`, remove every call site across all component config_flows, not just a representative sample.
item.content: Search the whole repo (e.g. `grep -rn '_set_confirm_only' homeassistant/components`) and delete each call in every integration's config_flow.py. Hidden tests likely assert no remaining callers, so partial removal fails.

item.title: Turn removed API into a reporting no-op
item.description: Instead of deleting `_set_confirm_only` outright, keep it as a no-op that reports usage, raising for core integrations and ignoring custom ones.
item.content: Implement the method to call `report_usage` with a core-integration flag so core code that reintroduces the call fails loudly while custom integrations are tolerated. This preserves backward compatibility for third-party code.

item.title: Remove the context key from the type definition
item.description: Dropping a flow-context flag requires removing the key from `ConfigFlowContext` TypedDict, not just the setter.
item.content: Delete the `confirm_only` key from `ConfigFlowContext` in the config_entries flow module so type checking and any context serialization no longer reference it. Leaving the key behind leaves dead schema.

item.title: Deprecate YAML config with issue registry
item.description: When deprecating YAML import for an integration, create a repair issue in async_setup rather than silently ignoring config.
item.content: In async_setup, if DOMAIN is in config, call async_create_issue with HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN, issue_id f"deprecated_yaml_{DOMAIN}", translation_key="deprecated_yaml", is_fixable=False, issue_domain=DOMAIN, and translation_placeholders containing domain and integration_title. Set breaks_in_ha_version to a future release.

item.title: Test deprecation issues via issue_registry fixture
item.description: Verify the deprecation warning by asserting the issue exists in the issue registry after setting up the component from YAML.
item.content: Write a test that patches the integration's update/network call, calls async_setup_component with a YAML config dict, awaits hass.async_block_till_done(), then asserts issue_registry.async_get_issue(domain=HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN, issue_id=f"deprecated_yaml_{DOMAIN}") is truthy.

item.title: Import DOMAIN alias for Home Assistant core domain
item.description: When creating issues, the issue domain must be the Home Assistant core domain, which conflicts with the integration's own DOMAIN constant.
item.content: Import `from homeassistant.core import DOMAIN as HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN` to avoid shadowing the integration's DOMAIN, and pass HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN as the first argument to async_create_issue while setting issue_domain=DOMAIN.

item.title: Avoid caching mutable state dicts in entity constructors
item.description: Entities that store a reference to a state dict at init time will read stale data when the source replaces the dict.
item.content: Convert cached state attributes into @property methods that re-query the live source (e.g., roomba_reported_state(self.vacuum)) so entities always reflect current telemetry after the underlying dict is replaced.

item.title: Use truthiness checks for optional telemetry fields
item.description: Firmware may omit fields like 'name' in initial MQTT packets, causing loops to hang until timeout.
item.content: Wait on a non-empty reported state rather than a specific optional field, and apply a fallback (e.g., .get('name') or 'Roomba') so pairing succeeds when the field is absent.

item.title: Add regression tests for both timeout and dynamic state paths
item.description: Hidden tests verified both the missing-name pairing fallback and live state updates after dict replacement.
item.content: Write tests that simulate telemetry omitting optional fields and that replace the reported dict post-setup, asserting the config flow creates the entry and entity state updates accordingly.

item.title: Avoid testing internal helpers directly
item.description: The reviewer rejected a test that asserted on an internal implementation detail rather than public behavior.
item.content: When writing tests for a new platform, test observable entity state and registry snapshots (e.g., via snapshot tests of entity registry entries and states) instead of calling internal functions or asserting on private attributes. Reviewers consider tests of internals unnecessary.

item.title: Follow existing platform patterns in the integration
item.description: The accepted binary_sensor platform mirrored the integration's existing entity/description patterns.
item.content: Reuse the integration's existing entity base class, coordinator data types, and entity-description dataclass pattern (with a value_fn callable) so the new platform is consistent with sibling platforms like sensor and event.

item.title: Register new platforms and strings together
item.description: Adding a platform requires updating PLATFORMS, strings.json entity names, and tests/snapshots in one change.
item.content: When adding a new platform, add it to the PLATFORMS list in __init__.py, add translation keys under the entity section of strings.json, and include snapshot tests covering each entity's registry entry and state.

item.title: Parameterize error-scenario tests into one test
item.description: Reviewers prefer a single parameterized test covering all error scenarios over multiple separate tests.
item.content: When writing tests for multiple error/exception scenarios, use pytest.mark.parametrize with (error, expected_state, expected_flows) tuples and descriptive ids instead of separate test functions. Grouping scenarios into one test is explicitly preferred by Home Assistant reviewers.

item.title: Assert config entry state and flow sources for setup errors
item.description: For integration setup error tests, verify both ConfigEntryState and the resulting flow sources.
item.content: In setup error tests, set the API mock's side_effect to the exception, call setup_integration, then assert mock_config_entry.state equals the expected ConfigEntryState and that hass.config_entries.flow.async_progress() sources match expected (e.g. SOURCE_REAUTH for auth errors, empty for retry).

item.title: Distinguish retry vs reauth error handling
item.description: Map exception types to expected setup outcomes: most errors lead to SETUP_RETRY, auth errors to SETUP_ERROR with reauth flow.
item.content: Expect ConfigEntryState.SETUP_RETRY for PterodactylApiError, BadRequestError, ClientError, TimeoutError, and 500 ClientResponseError; expect SETUP_ERROR with a SOURCE_REAUTH flow for 401 ClientResponseError. Build ClientResponseError with request_info=Mock(real_url=URL(TEST_URL)), history=[], and status.

item.title: Map unknown enum values to None, not to options
item.description: When a sensor uses SensorDeviceClass.ENUM, the 'unknown' member must be excluded from options and mapped to None in the value function.
item.content: Build options from enum values excluding the UNKNOWN member, and have the value function return None when the state is None or UNKNOWN. Reviewers reject 'unknown' appearing in options because HA treats None as the unknown state.

item.title: Gate optional sensors on data availability
item.description: Only add entities whose underlying data is actually reported, e.g. skip AC power sensor when ac_connected is None.
item.content: Check coordinator data at setup time and conditionally append the entity description; desktops without mains supply should not get an AC power binary sensor. This avoids permanently-unknown entities.

item.title: Use per-item dynamic descriptions with closures for list data
item.description: For batteries/devices discovered in a list, generate entity descriptions per item with keys and translation placeholders derived from the item name.
item.content: Create descriptions with unique keys like f'battery_{name}', set translation_placeholders from the model/name, and bind the item name via default args in lambdas. Enable by default only for external devices (scope DEVICE), leaving system batteries disabled since main sensors cover them.

item.title: Migrate registry entries instead of breaking users
item.description: When moving entities to a new device, auto-migrate existing registry entries (names, areas, entity IDs) so the breaking change becomes a formality.
item.content: Before relocating entities to a new device, write a migration that transfers user customizations (custom name, area, entity_id) from the old device/entity entries to the new ones. Reviewers value narrow, well-justified migration gaps over user-visible breakage.

item.title: Scope new device identifiers to the config entry
item.description: Encode the config entry id plus a typed suffix in device identifiers so group devices can be parsed back and never collide with real device IEEE addresses.
item.content: Use a format like `{entry_id}_group_0x{group_id:04x}` and a strict regex (e.g. exactly four lowercase hex digits) when parsing, returning None for anything else. This lets helpers distinguish group devices from coordinator/device entries reliably.

item.title: Guard device-automation and diagnostics paths for synthetic devices
item.description: New synthetic devices (groups) flow through generic device code paths, so add early returns in device_trigger and diagnostics to avoid KeyErrors or wrong data.
item.content: When introducing a device type not backed by a real hardware device, audit shared entry points: return empty trigger lists for group devices in async_get_triggers, and branch diagnostics to return group-specific data. Also override entity name/device_info for group entities so they inherit the group device's name and info.

item.title: Translate exceptions with translation_domain/key/placeholders
item.description: Home Assistant quality scale exception-translations rule requires raising exceptions with translation metadata instead of hardcoded strings.
item.content: Replace `raise UpdateFailed(str(err))` with `raise UpdateFailed(translation_domain=DOMAIN, translation_key="update_error", translation_placeholders={...}) from err`. Keep the original exception chained via `from err` so raw details remain in logs.

item.title: Add exceptions section to strings.json
item.description: Exception translation keys must be defined under an `exceptions` block in the integration's strings.json.
item.content: Add `"exceptions": {"<key>": {"message": "... {placeholder} ..."}}` to strings.json, using the same key referenced in translation_key and matching placeholder names.

item.title: Update quality_scale.yaml rule status
item.description: When implementing a quality scale rule, flip its status in quality_scale.yaml from todo to done.
item.content: Locate the rule entry (e.g. `exception-translations: todo`) in the integration's quality_scale.yaml and change it to `done` as part of the same change.

item.title: Use placeholders for dynamic values in exception translations
item.description: Reviewers prefer interpolating variable data (IPs, ports, names) via translation_placeholders rather than embedding them in the translated message string.
item.content: When adding exception translations, keep the message template static and pass all dynamic values (addresses, ports, names) as placeholders. This avoids invalidating translations when values change and keeps untranslatable data out of the string.

item.title: Chain original exceptions with 'from err' when translating
item.description: When replacing hardcoded exception messages with translation keys, preserve the underlying error via exception chaining.
item.content: Raise the translated exception with `from err` so the original exception text remains available in logs, even though the user-facing message no longer includes it.

item.title: Add exception translation keys to strings.json
item.description: Exception translations require corresponding entries under an 'exceptions' section in the integration's strings.json.
item.content: Define each translation_key used in code under `"exceptions"` in strings.json with a `message` field, and reference it via `translation_domain=DOMAIN, translation_key=..., translation_placeholders={...}`.

item.title: Share location dispatch between user and reconfigure steps
item.description: Extract the location-type branching into a helper reused by both the user and reconfigure steps to avoid duplication.
item.content: Create a private helper like _async_handle_location(step_id, data_schema, location_type, api_key) that sets self._data and dispatches to coordinates/country/validate steps. Pass the step_id through so validation errors render on the correct form.

item.title: Prefill reconfigure forms from entry data
item.description: When source is SOURCE_RECONFIGURE, derive suggested values from the existing entry rather than defaults.
item.content: Detect the current location type by checking CONF_COUNTRY_CODE / CONF_LATITUDE in entry data, and use add_suggested_values_to_schema to prefill. For coordinates, return entry coordinates instead of hass.config defaults when reconfiguring.

item.title: Replace entry data on reconfigure to drop stale keys
item.description: Use async_update_reload_and_abort with the new data so keys from the previous location type are removed.
item.content: When finishing a reconfigure flow, replace the entry data entirely (not merge) so leftover keys like CONF_COUNTRY_CODE or CONF_LATITUDE from the old location type don't persist. Keep the entry title unchanged and mark reconfiguration-flow done in the quality scale.

item.title: Normalize stored timestamps to local tz before seeding cron iterators
item.description: Timestamps loaded from storage carry a fixed UTC offset, so seeding a long-lived CronSim with them pins the schedule to that offset across DST changes.
item.content: When seeding a cron iterator that lives for the process lifetime, convert the seed with dt_util.as_local so wall-clock computation follows the configured time zone. Seeds already local (like now) are unaffected, so the conversion is safe to apply unconditionally.

item.title: Test DST bugs in both directions with frozen time
item.description: A DST offset bug can manifest differently in spring and autumn, so parametrize tests over both transitions.
item.content: Seed storage with a timestamp carrying the old offset, set the time zone to a DST-observing zone like Europe/Amsterdam, and assert both the reported next time and the actual firing time at the configured local wall-clock time. Include a check just before the scheduled time to confirm no early fire.

item.title: Check whether a stored-value bug also affects other consumers
item.description: Reviewers asked whether fixing only the cron iterator leaves the stored timestamp wrong for other readers such as the frontend.
item.content: Before settling on a narrow fix, trace where the stored value is consumed (API responses, UI display, other scheduling paths) and confirm the fix covers the user-visible symptom. Document that reasoning in the PR so reviewers can accept the scope.

item.title: Use channel_index/channel_condition for multi-channel Tuya entities
item.description: When splitting Tuya multi-channel device entities into per-channel child devices, replace indexed translation keys with channel_index and channel_condition fields.
item.content: Instead of separate entity descriptions with indexed translation keys and placeholders (e.g. 'indexed_current' with index '1'/'2'), define one description per channel using channel_index=N and a channel_condition callable that checks the device's status_range for the second channel DPCode. This lets the TuyaEntity base class route entities to child devices automatically.

item.title: Factor per-channel entity descriptions into a helper function
item.description: Generate repeated per-channel sensor descriptions with a small builder function rather than duplicating blocks.
item.content: Create a helper like _meter_channel_sensors(channel) returning a tuple of TuyaSensorEntityDescription objects built with f-string DPCode keys (e.g. DPCode(f'cur_power{channel}')). This keeps the diff compact and ensures all channels share identical device_class/state_class/unit settings.

item.title: Check status_range for channel presence detection
item.description: Detect multi-channel capability by checking whether the second channel's DPCode exists in device.status_range.
item.content: Use a predicate such as `DPCode.CUR_POWER2 in device.status_range` (or WARN_POWER2 for numbers) as the channel_condition to gate channel entities. This avoids creating channel entities on single-channel devices that share the same category.

item.title: Use next_name_part to detect device-named entities
item.description: When an entity has no name of its own, check entry.next_name_part is NextNamePart.DEVICE before falling back to the device name.
item.content: Entity registry entries expose next_name_part; only fall back to the device name when it equals NextNamePart.DEVICE, otherwise the entity's name comes from another source (area, etc.) and the device name would be wrong.

item.title: Prefer name_by_user over name for device fallback
item.description: When returning a device's name as a fallback, use device.name_by_user or device.name to respect user overrides.
item.content: Device registry entries have both name and name_by_user; users rename devices via name_by_user, so always prefer it with `device.name_by_user or device.name` to match what the UI shows.

item.title: Add keyword-only flags to template functions
item.description: New optional template function parameters should be keyword-only with a default preserving existing behaviour.
item.content: Define new flags as `*, fallback: bool = False` so existing templates are unaffected and the flag is explicit at call sites; also test both direct-call and filter (`| entity_name(fallback=True)`) forms.

item.title: Implement backup agent listener registration pattern
item.description: Backup agents must notify the backup integration when agents are added/removed via a listener mechanism.
item.content: Implement async_register_backup_agents_listener storing listeners in hass.data under a DATA_BACKUP_AGENT_LISTENERS key, and call them from async_setup_entry via entry.async_on_state_change. This is the standard pattern for backup platforms to signal agent availability changes.

item.title: Chunk large uploads for proxy compatibility
item.description: Uploading backups in fixed-size chunks avoids body-size limits imposed by proxies like Cloudflare.
item.content: Split uploads into ~50 MiB chunks (below the 100 MB Cloudflare limit) and report progress via OnProgressCallback. Stream downloads rather than buffering whole files in memory.

item.title: Wrap platform errors in BackupAgentError with translations
item.description: Backup agent methods should convert library-specific exceptions into BackupAgentError with translation keys.
item.content: Use a decorator that catches the client library's timeout and generic errors and re-raises BackupAgentError with translation_domain=BACKUP_DOMAIN and appropriate translation_key, so the backup UI shows meaningful messages instead of raw exceptions.

item.title: Remove availability overrides to inherit coordinator availability
item.description: When entities hardcode available=True and only flag staleness via assumed_state, the frontend shows stale readings as live; deleting the overrides lets the passive coordinator's availability propagate.
item.content: For passive Bluetooth integrations, don't override `available` to always return True and don't rely on `assumed_state` to signal stale data—the frontend gives no visual hint for it. Remove the overrides so entities inherit the coordinator's availability and become unavailable after the stale-advertisement window.

item.title: Subclass passive coordinator to add missing transition logging
item.description: The passive Bluetooth coordinator doesn't log when a device stops or resumes broadcasting, so subclass it to log each transition once.
item.content: Override `_async_handle_unavailable` and `_async_handle_bluetooth_event` in a coordinator subclass, guarding with a boolean flag so each transition logs exactly once. This satisfies the Silver `log-when-unavailable` rule and keeps the quality_scale.yaml comment accurate.

item.title: Open linked docs follow-up before merging behavior changes
item.description: A reviewer asked for the documentation follow-up to be opened and linked before merge when behavior diverges from the docs' data update description.
item.content: When a fix changes documented behavior (e.g. sensors now going unavailable), open the docs PR against `next` and link it in the PR description before merging, rather than promising a follow-up later.

item.title: Prefer descriptive enum member names over abbreviations
item.description: When introducing a new enum, reviewers may reject abbreviated member names like CUR in favor of full words like CURRENT.
item.content: When creating enum members, use full descriptive names (CURRENT, MAX) rather than abbreviations (CUR) even if the underlying string value stays the same. Reviewers flag abbreviations as unclear, and the enum is the right place to improve naming.

item.title: Keep constants that external integrations import
item.description: Before removing a constant, check whether custom integrations import it; keep it even if unused internally.
item.content: When cleaning up unused constants, distinguish truly unused ones from those imported by external/custom integrations. Remove only the former; keep the latter (e.g. ATTR_LAST_TRIGGERED) to avoid breaking third-party code.

item.title: Replace string literals with enum members in tests too
item.description: When adding a state attribute enum, update both entity code and tests to reference the enum instead of raw strings.
item.content: After introducing a state attribute enum, replace raw string keys in extra_state_attributes, restore logic, and test assertions with the enum members. This keeps tests aligned with the new pattern and catches mismatches.

item.title: Use TYPE_CHECKING for type-narrowing asserts
item.description: Reviewers require assert statements used only for type narrowing to be guarded by TYPE_CHECKING so they don't run at runtime.
item.content: When you need an assert to narrow an Optional type for mypy (e.g. asserting entry.unique_id is not None), wrap it in `if TYPE_CHECKING:` and import TYPE_CHECKING from typing. This avoids runtime asserts while satisfying the type checker.

item.title: Redact PII in diagnostics
item.description: Diagnostics for BLE integrations must omit addresses, unique IDs, and device names that embed MAC digits.
item.content: When adding diagnostics, exclude the device address, unique_id, config entry data, and any name/title containing MAC fragments. Expose only non-identifying data like RSSI, manufacturer/service data as hex, and parsed sensor values.

item.title: Test diagnostics with snapshots and no-advertisement case
item.description: Cover both the normal advertisement path and the case where no advertisement has been received using syrupy snapshots.
item.content: Write a test that injects a Bluetooth service info and compares get_diagnostics_for_config_entry output to a snapshot, plus a second test asserting the diagnostics structure when no advertisement exists (service_info and parsed_advertisement are None).
